bibliographic_scope.title: Hydrothermal Synthesis of Weakly Agglomerated Nanocrystalline Scandia-Stabilized Zirconia
bibliographic_scope.authors: Gang Xu; Yawen Zhang; Chunsheng Liao; Chunhua Yan
bibliographic_scope.journal: Journal of the American Ceramic Society

interpretations.topic: Two concentrations and two composition bases
interpretations.text: The target is 8 mol% Sc2O3-stabilized zirconia on an oxide basis. The method separately prints nominal starting values of 92 mol% ZrO(NO3)2 and 16 mol% Sc(NO3)3. Those literal feed values are not two normalized percentages summing to 100, nor an 8 mol% scandium-cation fraction. Total cation concentration is separate from urea concentration. The stock solvent and individual nitrate charges are not specified.

The authors attribute the low-temperature stage to slow urea hydrolysis and homogeneous co-precipitation before crystallization at 180 °C. They propose polymeric/hydrous-oxide intermediates and a more ordered precursor; these are mechanistic interpretations, not measured transient species or molecular structures. Direct 180 °C treatment gives more monoclinic phase.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 2, Results and Discussion; Figure 2

interpretations.text: The first-page discussion describes pure cubic material for urea ≤0.5 mol/L. The conclusion uses <0.5 mol/L, and Figure 2a shows a small nonzero monoclinic point at 0.5 mol/L. The 0.5 mol/L route therefore retains an unresolved phase-purity boundary rather than a blanket pure-cubic label or an invented exact fraction.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 1–3, Results, Figure 2a and Conclusions

interpretations.topic: The short concentration series is a separate schedule
interpretations.text: Figure 3 uses 80 °C for 24 h followed by 180 °C for 48 h, at 0.05, 0.1, 0.25 and 0.5 mol/L total cations with cation:urea = 1:4. The long urea series uses 48 h followed by 72 h. The 0.5 mol/L cation endpoint with that ratio is not silently reconciled with the general 0.1–1.5 mol/L urea range. Individual phase fractions for Figure 3 are not tabulated.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Experimental Procedure and Figure 3

interpretations.topic: Three size estimates describe different observables
interpretations.text: For 0.05 mol/L cations and 0.2 mol/L urea after the long schedule, TEM gives an average grain size below 10 nm, XRD linewidth analysis gives 7.0 nm, and BET gives a specific surface area of 157 m²/g with an author-calculated equivalent size of 6 nm. These are separate analytical quantities, not repeated TEM diameters. Figure 5 shows a 50 nm scale bar.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 3, Figure 5 and morphology/XRD/BET paragraph

interpretations.topic: Calcination retains cubic phase while promoting grain growth
interpretations.text: The paper reports cubic phase retention during 1 h calcination under stagnant air over 600–1200 °C. Grain size changes little below 800 °C and grows substantially above 1000 °C, reaching a text-reported XRD crystallite size of 36.5 nm at 1200 °C. Other Figure 6 point ordinates are preserved visually without extracting exact numbers.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 1, 3, Experimental Procedure, calcination paragraph and Figure 6

interpretations.topic: Solution pH and applications are separate scopes
interpretations.text: Figure 4 shows increasing final solution pH and decreasing XRD crystallite size as urea concentration rises. The plotted pH and size ordinates are not tabulated here. The paper motivates solid-oxide fuel-cell electrolytes through cited literature but supplies no conductivity measurement for these powders.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Introduction and Figure 4

experimental_scope.source_feed_composition: 92 mol% ZrO(NO3)2 and 16 mol% Sc(NO3)3, printed nominal feed; retained literally.
experimental_scope.solvent: Not separately specified for stock preparation.
experimental_scope.drying: Vacuum oven at approximately 40 °C; duration and pressure unreported.
experimental_scope.calcination: 600–1200 °C for 1 h, muffle furnace, stagnant air.

analytical_contexts.conditions: Cu Kα radiation; average crystallite size from (111) linewidth using the cited Scherer formula. No peak-fit parameters or shape factor reported.
analytical_contexts.phase_fraction: Relative areas of monoclinic (−111) and (111), compared with those plus the cubic (111) contribution; source notation retained in the main. No independent reanalysis.

analytical_contexts.conditions: Morphology and size; no accelerating voltage or specimen-dispersion recipe supplied.
Specific surface area; degassing conditions and conversion assumptions not specified.
Solution after hydrothermal treatment; measurement temperature not reported.

source_conflicts: At 0.5 mol/L urea, main p. 1 says pure cubic for ≤0.5 mol/L, while the conclusion says <0.5 mol/L. Figure 2a also shows a small nonzero monoclinic point at 0.5 mol/L. Preserve the boundary uncertainty, without an exact digitized fraction.

The general method gives urea concentrations 0.1–1.5 mol/L; Figure 3 includes 0.5 mol/L cations at a cation:urea ratio of 1:4, which implies a value outside that general range. Retain the explicit cation setting and ratio without silently changing either statement.
limitations: Full supplied three-page main only; local SI not located or verified and cited full sources unreviewed.

Stock-solution solvent, stock preparation order, individual nitrate charges, hydration states, heating ramps, pressure, cooling details, filter specification, wash doses/repetitions, drying duration/pressure and storage are not reported.
The source prints 92 mol% ZrO(NO3)2 and 16 mol% Sc(NO3)3 as nominal feed composition. These are retained literally, not normalized to a sum of 100 or confused with 8 mol% Sc2O3 oxide composition.
The Figure 3 series uses 80 °C for 24 h then 180 °C for 48 h. It must not inherit the 48 h + 72 h schedule of Figures 1, 2a, 4, 5 and 6.
Only the 0.05 mol/L cation / 0.2 mol/L urea long-schedule specimen has the text-reported TEM, XRD and BET sizes. No approximate graph coordinates are converted to exact measurements.
No atomic coordinates, refined unit cell, measured conductivity or sintering-performance dataset is supplied. Molecular/specimen and apparatus graphics are illustrative; presentation pending.
